terms.meaning: a question sent to the search service
a rule that limits the search to one folder or one file type
a list box from which the owner picks one item
a function that reacts when a keyboard key is pressed

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the question form
sections.what: Brings in the state tool, the icons, the query function and the answer and evidence display parts.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form needs these to read input, call the server and show results.

sections.name: QuerySectionProps
sections.title: Input type for query section
sections.what: Declares that the section receives the list of collections indexed in this visit.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the dropdown offer only collections the owner has just indexed.
sections.watch_out: The list only includes collections indexed during this visit, so collections from earlier visits are missing.

sections.name: QuerySection (part 1)
sections.title: Question state and submit logic
sections.what: Stores the question, collection, filters, result and error. When a question is submitted, trims it, sends it with the filters, the collection and a limit of ten passages, then stores the reply. The old result is cleared first.
sections.why: Likely reason: clearing the old result first stops an old answer from showing next to the loading message.
sections.watch_out: If the request fails, the old answer is already gone and only an error is shown.

sections.name: QuerySection: if
sections.title: Enter key sends and collection dropdown
sections.what: Sends the question when Enter is pressed without Shift, so Shift plus Enter can add a new line. Also draws the how-to box and the collection dropdown, which lists Default and any collections indexed during this visit.
sections.why: Likely reason: Enter to send is a common habit in chat tools, and Shift plus Enter keeps longer questions possible.
sections.watch_out: The Enter behaviour only works if the question box calls this handler, and that part of the layout is not in the packet.

sections.name: QuerySection (part 3)
sections.title: Question box and optional filters
sections.what: Shows the question box, a button that shows or hides the search filters, and two optional filters: a folder path and a file type. Pressing Enter starts a search, and Shift plus Enter adds a new line.
sections.why: Likely reason: the box and filters are turned off while a search runs, so the question cannot change mid-search.
sections.watch_out: The file type choices must match the file type names the backend stores, or a filter returns nothing, and this file does not check that.

sections.name: QuerySection (part 4)
sections.title: Search button, errors and results
sections.what: Shows the Search and Answer button, which is off when the question is empty or a search is running. While waiting, it shows an Analyzing message. It then shows any error text and the answer and evidence panels.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocks empty or repeated searches and gives the user feedback while the backend works.
sections.watch_out: The error text is shown exactly as the backend sends it, so technical messages can reach the user.

summary: The ask-questions tab: a collection dropdown, a question box, optional filters, and the answer and evidence shown after a search. Only the first part of the file is visible in this packet.
purpose: Lets the owner type a question and get a sourced answer from the indexed documents.
why: Likely reason: asking questions is the main use of the app, so the question form and results sit together.
how: Holds the question, collection, filters, result and error values. When the owner submits, it sends the trimmed question, any folder or file type filters, the collection and a limit of 10 passages. It shows a spinner while waiting and stores the reply. Pressing Enter sends the question. The layout then draws the collection dropdown. The filters, the question box and the results are drawn in parts not shown in this packet.
inputs: The question text, the collection choice, the folder and file type filters, and the collections list from the page.
outputs: A request to the server, and a stored result for the answer and evidence cards.
risks: Each new question clears the previous result first, so earlier answers disappear. The number of passages is fixed at ten. Errors show only the server's detail text. A filter toggle exists in the code, but its use is not visible here.
debug: If a question returns nothing, check the selected collection and that indexing finished. If an error appears, read the message in the error box. If Enter does nothing, check that the question box calls the key handler, which is in code not shown here.
